prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour Party Manifesto 2017 – Summary (under 500 words)

Vision: Build a fairer Britain that “works for the many, not the few” by tackling inequality, improving living standards, investing in modern infrastructure, and protecting quality public services. Pursue a jobs-first Brexit.

Economy, tax and finance
- £250bn National Transformation Fund over 10 years for transport, energy, digital and science; HS2 to Scotland; Crossrail 2; Northern Powerhouse Rail; nationwide rail electrification; universal superfast broadband by 2022 and 5G on major routes.
- Industrial Strategy with missions: 60% of energy from zero/renewables by 2030; reach 3% of GDP on R&D; skills via a National Education Service.
- National Investment Bank and regional development banks to finance SMEs, co-ops and long-term innovation.
- Fair tax: no rises in income tax for 95% (below £80k), no NICs/VAT hikes; higher taxes for top 5% and large corporations; restore small profits rate; crack down on avoidance; eliminate the day-to-day deficit within five years while investing (Fiscal Credibility Rule).

Ownership, business and consumers
- Expand co-ops; employee “right to own” on sales; insource public services.
- Public ownership: bring rail back as franchises expire; take energy networks and water into public ownership; reverse Royal Mail privatisation.
- Tougher procurement standards (tax, labour, environment), curb late payments; strengthen corporate governance; excessive pay levy and pay ratio conditions for public contractors.

Energy and climate
- Emergency cap to keep average dual-fuel bills below £1,000; insulate 4m homes; interest-free loans for homeowners; better standards for rentals.
- Ban fracking; support renewables, tidal, CCS and nuclear; protect North Sea jobs; align with Paris targets; maintain Euratom/access to internal energy market.

Brexit, immigration and trade
- Accept result; prioritise jobs and living standards; retain benefits of Single Market/Customs Union; guarantee EU nationals’ rights; reject “no deal”; meaningful parliamentary vote; no hard Irish border; devolve returning powers.
- Fair, needs-based migration system; end indefinite detention; stop exploitation; restore Migrant Impact Fund; welcome international students (not in targets); take fair share of refugees.
- Pro-trade with strong standards, transparency, and SME support; defend against dumping; no parallel ISDS courts.

Education and skills (National Education Service)
- Early years: expand and fund high-quality childcare; extend 30 free hours to all 2‑year‑olds; strengthen Sure Start.
- Schools: reverse cuts; fair funding; class sizes under 30 for infants; free primary meals; reduce teaching-to-test; support SEND; tackle workload; end pay cap.
- Further/Adult: free lifelong FE (incl. ESOL); restore EMA; replace loans/fees; invest in colleges and T‑levels.
- Apprenticeships: maintain levy, improve quality and completion; widen access.
- Higher Ed: abolish tuition fees; restore maintenance grants.

Work, rights and social security
- 20‑point plan: £10 Living Wage by 2020; ban zero-hours; sectoral bargaining; repeal Trade Union Act; end public sector pay cap; four new public holidays; abolish tribunal fees; stronger equality, parental and bereavement rights; clamp down on bogus self-employment.
- Pensions: retain triple lock; protect universal pensioner benefits; address WASPI injustice; review pension age fairly; cut fees.
- Social security: scrap sanctions, bedroom tax; reform UC; boost ESA (+£30), Carer’s Allowance; end private assessments; embed UNCRPD.

Housing
- Over 1m homes; at least 100k council/HA homes per year by end of Parliament; new Dept for Housing; new towns; protect green belt.
- Private renters: three‑year tenancies as norm; cap in-line rent rises; ban letting fees; minimum standards; restore HB for 18–21s; suspend RTB unless like‑for‑like replacement.

Health and care
- NHS: £30bn extra; end privatisation; repeal HSCA; safe staffing; scrap pay cap; restore bursaries; free parking; faster treatment (18 weeks, A&E 4 hours); ring‑fence mental health; expand children’s MH and school counselling.
- Social care: foundation of a National Care Service; +£8bn over Parliament (+£1bn year one); ethical care standards; raise Carer’s Allowance; move to lifetime cost cap and fairer funding via cross‑party consensus.

Safety, justice and communities
- 10,000 extra police; domestic/sexual violence commissioner, national refuge fund; review Prevent; 500 border guards; 3,000 firefighters; halt cuts; flood duty.
- Justice: restore key legal aid, curb fees, no‑fault divorce, inquiries into historic injustices; 3,000 more prison officers; end probation privatisation.
- Transport: public railway with fare caps and better staffing; re‑regulate buses/enable municipal firms; invest in cycling/walking; fair taxi/PHV rules.

Environment, culture, media, sport, democracy
- Clean Air Act; protect habitats; ban neonicotinoids; plant 1m trees; end badger cull; tougher cruelty sentences.
- £1bn Cultural Capital Fund; arts pupil premium; keep BBC independent, Channel 4 public; implement Leveson recommendations.
- Fans’ rights in football; anti‑touting measures.
- Constitutional Convention; votes at 16; Lords reform; extend FOI; tougher lobbying rules.

Nations and the world
- Oppose Scottish indyref2; strengthen devolution; uphold Good Friday.
- Foreign policy based on human rights and international law; recognise Palestine; suspend arms to Saudi pending UN probe; NATO 2% and renew Trident; defence industrial strategy.
- Maintain 0.7% aid; tackle tax havens; refugee strategy; promote universal health coverage globally.
